entries.title: US-Iran talks begin in Switzerland as Tehran says it closed Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: The US disputed Iran's claim the waterway is shut, a move Tehran says was a response to Israeli attacks in Lebanon.

entries.title: Fuel sales halted in occupied Crimea as Ukraine targets oil facilities
entries.snippet: Fuel had already been rationed due to shortages caused by Kyiv's attacks against supply routes in Russian-occupied territories.

entries.title: Colombia's escalating, brutal internal conflict is defining its presidential election
entries.snippet: A left-wing senator who backs talks with armed gangs faces an outsider endorsed by Trump.

entries.title: France bans alcohol at music festival events under red heatwave alert
entries.snippet: Annual street parties attended by millions ordered to help “preserve” healthcare services in 40C (104F) heat.

entries.title: Former Olympian denies vandalising Washington Reflecting Pool after arrest
entries.snippet: Davey Hearn says he was simply touching the new paint at the site out of curiosity and did not remove or alter it.

entries.title: Tight security as Indian students resit medical exam after alleged paper leak
entries.snippet: Millions of candidates face biometric checks and frisking as air force deployed to secure exam papers.

entries.title: Israeli strikes kill six people in Gaza including Al Jazeera cameraman, officials say
entries.snippet: The Israeli military accused Ahmed Wishah of being a "Hamas sniper operative", without providing evidence.

entries.title: Dutch royals enjoy two big results in one World Cup day
entries.snippet: There may be about 5,000 miles between the Netherlands and their former colony Curacao but members of the Dutch royal family managed to see both sides play on Saturday.

entries.title: African and Caribbean nations call for formal apology for transatlantic slavery
entries.snippet: The leaders have asked for apologies from the countries that benefited from the slave trade, as well as debt relief and financial compensation.

entries.title: Indian cricketer, 15, hits record-breaking 50 in just 11 balls
entries.snippet: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks the record for the fastest 50-over List A half-century in history on the same day he was not included in India's one-day international squad.

entries.title: Meloni tells Trump to 'focus on your own popularity' as row escalates
entries.snippet: The US president earlier questioned Meloni's popularity after suggesting she "begged" for a photo at G7 summit

entries.title: Zelensky returns highest Polish honour after award stripped
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president said his country was open to "engagement" about "difficult and painful chapters of our shared past".

entries.title: Lebanese turtle conservationist Mona Khalil killed by Israeli strike
entries.snippet: Mona Khalil, who had refused to leave the beach she had spent years protecting, died after several days in hospital, an environmental group said.

entries.title: US to stop funding HIV programmes in South Africa
entries.snippet: More than eight million South Africans are living with HIV – the highest number of any country in the world.

entries.title: Australia confirms first case of H5N1 bird flu as virus reaches every continent
entries.snippet: Australia was previously the only continent where the H5N1 bird flu strain had not yet been found.

entries.title: Bolivian president declares state of emergency
entries.snippet: The move comes after weeks of anti-government protests that have caused a shortage of basic goods in Bolivia.

entries.title: Tourist dies in Dominican Republic luxury resort fire
entries.snippet: Nearly 1,700 people were evacuated from the huge blaze at Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach in Bayahibe, a popular resort town on the Caribbean coast.

entries.title: James Burrows, legendary director of Cheers and Friends, dies aged 85
entries.snippet: Best-known as co-creator of sitcom Cheers, Burrows directed more than 1,000 episodes of other classics including the Big Bang Theory and Will and Grace.

entries.title: Boy, 12, wins hearts after trying to check sick chicken into Ethiopian hospital
entries.snippet: Markos's beloved hen was not responding to any treatments - so he did the only thing he could think of.

entries.title: Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi to stand trial for rape
entries.snippet: French prosecutors confirm Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi will stand trial for rape, in accusations dating back to 2023.

entries.title: A new survey on dads found that 9 out of 10 had a surprising reaction to fatherhood
entries.snippet: Men are traditionally thought of as providers for their children. But a report that interviewed thousands of fathers found them embracing another role.

entries.title: Freed from Cambodia's scam compounds, trafficking victims face a new crisis
entries.snippet: Cambodia's crackdown on scam centers has created a secondary crisis: thousands of stranded foreign workers are now roaming the streets of Phnom Penh.

entries.title: Want to improve your agility? Try these 'explosive power' exercises
entries.snippet: These simple movements combine speed and strength to train your body's ability to rapidly generate force. They can also help prevent injury and boost agility.

entries.title: DOJ memo stokes fear among disability advocates of a return to institutionalization
entries.snippet: The Justice Department's opinion challenges civil rights protections that have long treated the institutionalization of disabled Americans as a last resort.

entries.title: Opinion: Algae doesn't care about our party lines
entries.snippet: President Trump's beautification project of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has become plagued with a robust algae bloom, despite a $14 million investment and a coating of "American flag blue."

entries.title: These nuns spent a lifetime helping others. In their last years, who will help them?
entries.snippet: The sisters of Uganda are teachers, health-care advocates and more. Those who are in their twilight of their life need help. Who will come to their aid?

entries.title: JD Vance arrives in Switzerland for talks with Iran over fragile peace deal
entries.snippet: JD Vance arrived in Switzerland on Sunday for talks with Iranian officials, hoping to consolidate the fragile interim deal to end the war and kickstart fresh discussions over Tehran's nuclear program.

entries.title: Palestinian-American kids find inspiration, and escape, on the soccer pitch
entries.snippet: A dozen miles away from the World Cup games in New York/ New Jersey Stadium, Palestinian-American kids turn to soccer as an escape from the realities of war.

entries.title: A California man's case highlights gaps in care and oversight at DHS detention centers
entries.snippet: Federal officers shot Ricardo Parias eight months ago during an ICE operation to detain him. His lawyer says he is still in pain, highlighting gaps in oversight and care in DHS facilities.

entries.title: James Burrows, director of classic shows 'Cheers' and 'Friends,' dies at 85
entries.snippet: Burrows spent his career behind the camera specializing in situation comedies. Few viewers recognized him or knew his name, other than to see it flash quickly on the screen in the opening credits. But they knew his work.

entries.title: U.S. and Iran to talk Sunday in Switzerland as Tehran says it closed Strait of Hormuz again
entries.snippet: U.S. and Iranian negotiators headed to a Swiss venue Saturday for talks on adding key details to their interim agreement to halt the war, hours after Tehran said it closed the Strait of Hormuz because of Israel's attacks in Lebanon and warned that little might be achieved if the

entries.title: Italian tourist killed in massive fire at Dominican Republic luxury beach resort
entries.snippet: The blaze at the Viva Dominicus Beach by Wyndham resort in Bayahibe — a popular destination for U.S. and international tourists on the Dominican Republic's southeastern coast — forced the evacuation of nearly 1,700 tourists and caused the death of an Italian national, authorities

entries.title: Extreme heat expected again at the Grand Canyon after 3 hikers die in heat-related incidents
entries.snippet: The U.S. National Weather Service issued an extreme heat watch at the Grand Canyon for midday Monday through Tuesday, forecasting temperatures that could reach or exceed 110 degrees Fahrenheit at the low-elevation Phantom Ranch.

entries.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 6, including 2 children and an Al Jazeera cameraman
entries.snippet: Despite an October ceasefire between Israel and the militant group Hamas, the enclave has seen near-daily Israeli attacks that have killed over 1,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.

entries.title: Pope Leo XIV exalts first American saint Cabrini as a model for Christians for her care of migrants
entries.snippet: Leo, who has clashed with the Trump administration over its migrant crackdown, urged young people in particular to learn about Cabrini's life and service, once again confirming history's first U.S. pope as the heir to Pope Francis in prioritizing the plight of migrants.

entries.title: Trump tries to blame Reflecting Poll woes on vandalism, without offering substantiation
entries.snippet: The paint is peeling from Washington's Reflecting Pool after the renovation ordered by President Donald Trump, and he is now alleging that someone damaged it intentionally.

entries.title: Spanish judge orders prime minister's wife to face corruption trial and surrender her passport
entries.snippet: Begoña Gómez is accused of using her position to influence government contracts given to a group of technology companies. The judge also accused her of the misuse of public funds in the hiring of a consultant and the inappropriate use of software while she was a professor at a pu

entries.title: Trump deepens the dustup with Italy's Meloni, who says his 'unprovoked attacks are senseless'
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump on Saturday lashed out at Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, insisting that she asked "over and over" for a photo with him at the recent Group of Seven summit and criticizing what he said was Italy's lack of cooperation during the Iran war.

entries.title: Zelenskyy returns Poland's highest honor after Polish leader revokes it in a spat over history
entries.snippet: Polish President Karol Nawrocki decided to strip Zelenskyy of the Order of the White Eagle over the Ukrainian leader's decision to name a military unit after a Ukrainian paramilitary organization accused of massacring Poles during World War II.

entries.title: Russia strikes an apartment block in Ukraine's city of Kharkiv, killing 1 person
entries.snippet: Russian guided bombs struck an apartment block in Ukraine's second-largest city of Kharkiv on Saturday, killing at least one person and injuring nine, including a 6-year-old, authorities said.

entries.title: Utah marks a year of battling measles, with no clear end in sight
entries.snippet: More than 680 people have gotten sick since the state's first outbreak began on June 20, 2025.

entries.title: Cuba passes sweeping free-market reforms in biggest economic shift since revolution
entries.snippet: Observers on Friday called Cuba's new free-market reforms the most sweeping economic overhaul of the island's communist economy since the Cuban revolution, as the grandson of former President Raúl Castro said in an interview that Cuba must seek to move its economy forward.

entries.title: Israel and Hezbollah agree to a ceasefire as deadly fighting threatens U.S.-Iran deal
entries.snippet: Heavy overnight fighting in southern Lebanon between Israel and Hezbollah militants threatened to derail the initial U.S.-Iran agreement to end the war. But a last-ditch effort to secure another ceasefire succeeded, for now, and the Americans and Iranians plan to meet soon to beg

entries.title: Former U.S. envoy outlines challenges in next phase of Iran negotiations
entries.snippet: What are the prospects that the Israeli-Hezbollah ceasefire will hold and for how long? For insight, Amna Nawaz spoke with Rob Malley. He was the U.S. Special Envoy for Iran during the Biden administration and was part of the team that negotiated the nuclear agreement with Iran d

entries.title: News Wrap: UK's Starmer says he will not 'walk away' amid threat to leadership
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he would not walk away from any threat to his leadership after a rival within the Labour Party won a seat in Parliament, there's been a flu outbreak at an Air Force base in Texas just weeks after the end of mandato

entries.title: Research shows weight-loss drugs may also reduce cancer risk
entries.snippet: A growing body of research suggests popular weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy may also help treat or prevent certain cancers. It's the latest unexpected benefit to be associated with GLP-1s, which are now taken by one-in-eight American adults. William Brangham reports.

entries.title: How the Obama Presidential Center offers a new vision for presidential legacies
entries.snippet: The Obama Presidential Center is now open to the public in Chicago. Former President Obama says he does not want the center to feel like a shrine or a museum, but rather a representation of an American story still being written. Ali Rogin discusses what Obama is seeking to commun

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's record-low economic approval rating
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the preliminary deal with Iran, President Trump's record-low approval rating on the economy and some Republicans in Congress breaking with Trump.

entries.title: Derrick Adams celebrates the joy of the Black American experience through art
entries.snippet: As the rainbow array outside Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art suggests, artist Derrick Adams is accentuating the positive. He celebrates contemporary Black life and culture, depicting leisure, freedom and the pursuit of happiness. Jared Bowen of GBH Boston recently sat down

entries.title: U.S. advances to World Cup knockout round after win against Australia
entries.snippet: The U.S. team secured its spot in the World Cup's knockout round with a win against Australia on Friday. It's the first time since 1930 that the American men have won consecutive World Cup matches. To discuss the tournament, Amna Nawaz spoke with soccer writer Leander Schaerlaeck

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany could scrap law banning insults against politicians
entries.snippet: Germany's special law prohibiting the insulting of politicians has led to cases that many people consider absurd. Some members of the government want to abolish the law; others think there's a good reason to retain it.

entries.title: Ukraine hits Russia-controlled Crimea in deadly drone attack
entries.snippet: Footage of fires at a major depot on Crimea circulated on social media. The Moscow-aligned governor of Crimea has halted public fuel sales after the attack.

entries.title: Sudan: UN warns of mass atrocities in El-Obeid
entries.snippet: The United Nations Security Council has called on the paramilitary RSF in Sudan to not launch an attack on the city of El-Obeid.

entries.title: US, Iran hold talks in Switzerland while Strait of Hormuz remains shut
entries.snippet: Officials from the United States and Iran have begun talks to shore up an interim deal to end the war. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Undav heroics help Germany beat Ivory Coast
entries.snippet: In Germany's second 2026 World Cup game, Deniz Undav helped Germany to a comeback win against Ivory Coast in Toronto.

entries.title: Terror police probe suspected anti-Muslim attacks in Edinburgh
entries.snippet: Counterterrorism police have taken charge after a series of violent attacks in the Scottish capital that left five men injured.

entries.title: Are Ukraine drones really exposing gaps in Russia's defense?
entries.snippet: Once seen as almost impenetrable, Russian air defenses are now under growing strain from Ukrainian drones. A recent attack on Moscow has reignited debate over Russian vulnerabilities.

entries.title: France bans alcohol during Fete de la Musique amid heat wave
entries.snippet: France is taking additional measures as millions of people gear up for Fete de la Musique under punishing temperatures.

entries.title: Spain: PM's wife must face corruption trial, judge rules
entries.snippet: A court in Madrid ruled that there is sufficient evidence against Begona Gomez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. The 55-year-old university director is banned from leaving the country.

entries.title: Zelenskyy returns Poland's highest honor as row deepens
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president has returned a medal to Poland after a decision to strip him of the country's highest honor. Warsaw has been one of Kyiv's key allies since Russia began its war in Ukraine.

entries.title: India news: Millions of students retake NEET amid protests
entries.snippet: Some 2.2 million premedical aspirants are retaking the high-pressure entrance test across India under strict security measures. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Modi is in Kolkata for International Yoga Day. DW has more.

entries.title: Germany news: Pension overhaul may push retirement age to 70
entries.snippet: Germany is weighing sweeping pension changes, including raising the retirement age to 70. Meanwhile, football fans are celebrating after the men's national side qualified for the World Cup knockout stage. DW has more.

entries.title: Iran says it's closing Strait of Hormuz again
entries.snippet: Iran's joint military command said the strait had been closed due to Israel's continued attacks in Lebanon. Meanwhile, Iran's negotiators are heading to Switzerland for Iran-US talks on their interim deal.

entries.title: Pakistan: Roadside bombs kill 7 in northwest
entries.snippet: A police officer said twin blasts in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province were triggered remotely. No group immediately claimed responsibility.

entries.title: Inequality is elementary to Germany's school system
entries.snippet: Children's paths through Germany's school system are often determined before their first day of kindergarten, according to the national report on education. An elementary school in Bonn is offering a new model for kids.

entries.title: Bolivia's Paz declares state of emergency over blockades
entries.snippet: President Rodrigo Paz says he has declared the state of emergency "to free the country's roads." Blockades have become a major tactic in weeks of intensifying protests to demand that the president resign.

entries.title: Woman killed, hundreds evacuate in Dominican Republic hotel fire
entries.snippet: A huge fire tore through a four-star beach resort in the Dominican Republic, killing one woman. About 1,700 tourists were evacuated as the fire appeared to destroy most of the hotel.

entries.title: First case of H5 bird flu confirmed in Australia
entries.snippet: A migratory seabird tested positive for the contagious H5 variant of avian influenza in Western Australia. Australia had been the only continent where H5 was not detected.

entries.title: Trump unveils interim Air Force One, a gift from Qatar
entries.snippet: A former Qatar-owned jumbo jet, converted into the new presidential aircraft, is nearly ready for service. Trump said it had been transformed into "a flying White House."
